Calculation of Tax to be paid

| SI No. | Particulars | GST Paid/ITC Claimed (₹) | Tax to be paid |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Sale of machinery after 2 years | 7,20,000 | ₹ 4,50,000: Section 18(6) of CGST Act, 2017: When capital goods on which ITC has been taken are supplied, the registered person shall pay an amount equal to the higher of: 1. ITC taken on such capital goods reduced by 5% per quarter or part thereof, or 2. Tax on the transaction value of such supply. ITC originally claimed $= \text{₹ }7{,}20{,}000$. Period held: 01/04/2022 to 15/01/2025 = 12 quarters. Hence $\text{₹ }7{,}20{,}000 - 4{,}32{,}000\ (5\%\text{ per }12\text{ quarters} = 60\%) = 2{,}88{,}000$. Or Tax on Sale Value: $\text{₹ }25{,}00{,}000 * 18\% = 4{,}50{,}000$. Higher amount $= \text{₹ }4{,}50{,}000$ to be paid |
| 2 | Sale of car purchased 3 years back | 1,80,000 | ₹ 1,08,000: The registered person shall pay an amount equal to the higher of: 1. ITC taken on such capital goods reduced by 5% per quarter or part thereof, or 2. Tax on the transaction value of such supply. ITC originally claimed $= \text{₹ }1{,}80{,}000$. Period held: February 2022 to February 2025 = 13 quarters. Hence $\text{₹ }1{,}80{,}000 - 1.17.000\ (5\%\text{ per }13\text{ quarters}= 65\ \%) = 63{,}000$. Or Tax on Sale Value: $\text{₹ }6{,}00{,}000 * 18\% = 1{,}08{,}000$. Higher amount $= \text{₹ }1{,}08{,}000$ to be paid |

Note:
(1) The amount payable under Section 18(6) is treated as an output tax liability and to be reported in Form GSTR-1 and paid via Form GSTR-3B, rather than being shown as an ITC reversal in the ITC ledger.
(2) Generally ITC on Car is blocked but in the question specifically given that ITC claimed so we assumed that this is fall under the exceptions of the block credit.
